answer: Run a random-walk trust check over the agent interaction graph. Honest agents form a dense web where short walks mix fast, while a sybil farm sits behind a few attack edges, so walks from known-good seeds rarely spiral into it. Each walk's seed is committed as a hashed cipher before reveal, so nobody can steer it. Reward weight follows landing frequency: a lotus of fake accounts can bloom inside its own pond, but it cannot pull trust across that narrow cut.
